offsets._note: What people commonly RUN at each width — NOT a menu of what is orderable. Forged wheels are cut to the truck and the brands publish no ET, so this exists so the page can answer 'what offset?' with something real instead of silence. Every number carries its source. A width with no reliable public figure gets an explicit null, never a guess.
offsets._note_shape: Keyed on ROLE + WIDTH, not per model. Offset is set by rim width and axle position, not by spoke design — keying per model would be 756 copies of the same handful of numbers. The {min,max,typical} shape matches f450-fitment.json's rear.offsetMm so Fitment.geometry() could consume it unchanged.
offsets._note_bySize: An override layer for observed data points, not the primary key. 22x12 at -44 and 24x12 at -51 are two separate listings, not a rule about 12-inch wheels.

8.25.source: data/specs/f450-fitment.json — documented aftermarket dually range, bracketed by the OEM 19.5x6 ET+136

superSingle.label: Wide front
superSingle._note: GAP — nobody publishes wide-front offsets for dual-rear platforms. Mirrors f450-fitment.json's frontSuperSingle.offsetMm: null. Do NOT backfill these from the rear figures; the front axle is a different mounting position entirely.

f450.name: Ford F-450 Super Duty
f450._note_offsets: JTX builds the Dually Series to the truck and publishes no ET, so these are the offsets this platform actually runs — the documented aftermarket dually range, bracketed by the factory figure. They are the render's offsets, not a menu of anything orderable: a real order is spec'd with JTX.
f450._note_front: GAP: no public offset figures for wide front wheels on this platform. JTX's own pages say to call a salesperson, and no retailer publishes them. Left null on purpose — the UI says the front is spec'd to the truck rather than inventing a number. One call to JTX fills this in.
f450._note_body: Estimates until someone puts a tape on a truck — see vehicles.js. measured:false keeps the UI on words, not decimals.
